name: SentencePiece model training from command-line args + in-memory sentences
description:
SentencePieceTrainer::Train(args, sentences, serialized_model_proto) is the entry point that trains a new SentencePiece tokenizer model entirely from untrusted input: a command-line-style option string (`args`, e.g. "--model_type=bpe --vocab_size=8192 ...") and a vector of raw training sentences supplied directly in memory (wrapped by an internal VectorSentenceIterator). It is security relevant because `args` is parsed into protobuf TrainerSpec/NormalizerSpec fields via a generic key/value reflection-based setter, the sentences are tokenized/normalized/segmented character-by-character, and the resulting pieces/vocabulary are built and merged with complex priority-queue/suffix-array/EM algorithms (BPE merges, Unigram EM, word/char counting) - any of these stages can mishandle malformed option combinations, malformed UTF-8 sentences, pathological vocab sizes, tsv parsing, or precompiled normalizer charsmaps.
- sentencepiece::SentencePieceTrainer::Train(args, sentences, proto): target; builds a VectorSentenceIterator over `sentences` and calls the args+SentenceIterator overload, which parses `args` into kwargs, merges them into TrainerSpec/NormalizerSpec/denormalizer spec (MergeSpecsFromArgs/SetProtoField reflection parsing), populates the normalizer precompiled charsmap (PopulateNormalizerSpec/normalizer::Builder), selects a concrete Trainer implementation via TrainerFactory::Create based on `model_type`, and finally invokes TrainerInterface::Train()/LoadSentences() to run the chosen algorithm.
- sentencepiece::SentencePieceTrainer::Train(kwargs, sentences, proto): variant, same pipeline but takes a pre-split {key:value} kwargs map instead of a single args string, reaching the same MergeSpecsFromArgs/TrainerFactory/Trainer::Train core with a different parsing front-end (no need to split "--k=v" tokens, can supply arbitrary keys/values directly, including the special `_serialized_normalizer_spec` key).
- sentencepiece::SentencePieceTrainer::Train(args, SentenceIterator*, proto) and Train(kwargs, SentenceIterator*, proto): variants used internally by the two above; useful entries if the harness wants to supply a custom SentenceIterator instead of the vector<string> wrapper, exercising the same LoadSentences()/selector logic with a different sentence source.
- sentencepiece::SentencePieceTrainer::MergeSpecsFromArgs(args, trainer_spec, normalizer_spec, denormalizer_spec): source/config - parses the raw `args` option string, splitting on spaces and "=" and reflecting values onto TrainerSpec/NormalizerSpec proto fields (SetProtoField), including enum fields like model_type and numeric fields like vocab_size/character_coverage; can be fuzzed directly on arbitrary option strings to find parser bugs.
- sentencepiece::SentencePieceTrainer::GetNormalizerSpec(name): consumer/config helper that loads a named precompiled normalization charsmap (normalizer::Builder::GetPrecompiledCharsMap) that can be set into NormalizerSpec and fed back through Train, exercising the normalizer-building code path explicitly.
The input space is large and selected mainly from `args`/`kwargs` plus the sentence list: `model_type` selects which Trainer subclass runs (UNIGRAM default EM trainer, BPE greedy pair-merge trainer, WORD whitespace trainer, CHAR per-character trainer - each has a distinct core algorithm in C); `input_format` ("text" vs "tsv", where tsv requires "word\tfreq" lines parsed with absl::SimpleAtoi); `vocab_size`, `max_sentence_length`, `character_coverage`, `split_by_whitespace`, pretokenization flags, `shrinking_factor`, seed/pruning related flags (several controlled by ABSL flags like use_sparse_pruning/auto_character_coverage) change which branches of the per-model Train() loops execute; normalizer configuration (`normalization_rule_name`, `normalization_rule_tsv`, `add_dummy_prefix`, `escape_whitespaces`, `remove_extra_whitespaces`, `precompiled_charsmap`, `_serialized_normalizer_spec`) selects whether a built-in named charsmap, a user TSV-compiled charsmap, or a raw serialized NormalizerSpec is used, and these are mutually exclusive (checked by ContainsNormalizerKeys); and the raw bytes of each training sentence (arbitrary/invalid UTF-8, empty lines, lines containing the reserved UNK marker, overly long lines) drive the per-character/per-token symbol construction, pair-queue, and suffix structures inside each model's Train().
